newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian pleads guilty to 35 Port Arthur murders.
newsitem.headline: Australian pleads guilty to 35 Port Arthur murders.

text.p: Martin Bryant, the man accused of the worst mass killing in modern Australian history pleaded guilty on Thursday to all 35 murders, reversing his earlier plea of not guilty.
Bryant, 29, changed his plea to the April murders at the historic Port Arthur convict site during an appearance in the Supreme Court of Tasmania to discuss his trial on November 19.
Bryant laughed and smirked as he pleaded guilty to a total of 72 charges, including the 35 murders.
On April 28, a gunman opened fire on tourists at the Port Arthur tourist site on Tasmania's southeast coast. Bryant was arrested the following morning.
On September 30, Bryant pleaded not guilty to the murders and the other charges including attempted murder, grievous bodily harm, assault and arson.
Bryant appeared in court under heavy police protection, with the bomb squad sweeping the building before his appearance.
